title: Lesson 20 - Persistence-consistency scenarios: keys, natural keys, idempotent writes, upsert
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend techniques to ensure data is persisted consistently, including the design of keys (surrogate vs natural), idempotent write patterns, and upsert as the core integration persistence pattern.

questions.question: A nightly integration sometimes fails midway and is re-run. Which persistence pattern prevents duplicate records on re-run?
options: Insert with a duplicate rule alert
Upsert keyed on a stable external ID
Load with the Data Loader 'insert' operation
questions.explanation: Upsert on a stable external ID is idempotent - re-running updates existing records instead of creating duplicates; insert (A, D) duplicates on retry and delete-then-insert (C) risks data loss and churn.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about keys in Salesforce integration are TRUE?
options: The Salesforce record Id is stable across orgs
A mutable natural key risks duplicating records when it changes
An external ID enables upsert and cross-system identity
Surrogate keys are meaningful to external systems
questions.explanation: Mutable natural keys can duplicate on change (B) and external IDs enable upsert/identity (C); the Salesforce Id differs across orgs (A false) and a surrogate Id is not meaningful externally (D false).

questions.question: An integration loads Accounts then their Contacts across four source systems. What ordering/key design is best?
options: Upsert Accounts first (keyed on composite external ID), then Contacts resolving the parent by external ID
Insert all records in one parallel job without keys
Load only Accounts and skip Contacts
questions.explanation: Parent-first upsert with composite keys and parent resolution by external ID satisfies referential integrity and idempotency; other options break ordering or identity.
